## QUESTION 1

__Write an SQL query that pulls in the the salaries table and the collegeplaying table (and any other tables you might need) and store them in polars dataframes. In Python Polars, combine the dataframes to create a list of baseball players who attended BYU-Idaho. The new table should contain five columns: playerID, schoolID, salary, yearID and teamID associated with each salary.__

_I made sure to only select unique player IDs so there's no duplicate rows. Now I have 16 rows featuring the same two players again and again, but this is because the same player can be found on various different teams, with varying salaries, and playing across multiple years._

_AI use reflection_

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

salary = """
        SELECT playerID, salary, teamID, yearID
        FROM salaries;
        """

play = """
      SELECT playerID, schoolID
      FROM collegeplaying;
      """

players = pl.read_database(play, con)

salary = pl.read_database(salary, con)

players = players.unique("playerID")

```


```{python}
joined = players.join(salary, on="playerID", how="left")

joined = joined.filter(pl.col("schoolID") == "idbyuid")

joined
```

## QUESTION 2

1. Pick any two baseball teams and compare them using a metric of your choice (average salary, home runs, number of wins, etc). Be creative! Write an SQL query to read in the table(s) you need, then use polars to manipulate the data. Finally, make a graph using Lets-Plot to visualize the comparison. What do you learn?

_I chose to compare Washington Olympics versus Cleveland Forest Citys, and I was comparing the number of at-bats they both had. Side by side, you can see that Cleveland has had more total at-bats, winning over Washington by 411._

_AI use reflection_
**Link** to the original chat:
**The Process** How exactly did you use the tool?
**The Impact**  How did using AI impact your learning?

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
washington_olympics = """
        SELECT AB, teamID
        FROM batting
        WHERE teamID = "WS3";
        """

cleveland_forest_citys = """
      SELECT AB, teamID
      FROM batting
      WHERE teamID = "CL1";
      """

wo = pl.read_database(washington_olympics, con)

cfc = pl.read_database(cleveland_forest_citys, con)

wo = wo.group_by("teamID").agg(pl.col("AB").sum())

cfc = cfc.group_by("teamID").agg(pl.col("AB").sum())

both_teams = pl.concat([wo, cfc])

yipee = ggplot(both_teams, aes(x="teamID", y="AB")) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + labs(
        title="Team At-Bats",
        x="Team",
        y="Total At-Bats"
    )

yipee

```
